compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

Two rate-resolution defects in `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py`, both raised as
advisory findings by the review bot on Gerrit change 2984, patchset 7.

### 1. `_rate_for` assumes every usage-type body carries a region prefix (around line 180)

It normalizes with `body.split("-", 1)[1] if "-" in body else body`, discarding the first
hyphen-delimited segment as if it were always a region. A usage type without a region prefix, or a
model name whose leading segment is meaningful, is therefore normalized to the wrong key and priced
from the wrong rate or falls through to a fallback path that does not apply to it.

### 2. `_seed_for` has no fallback when a seed entry supplies only `input` (around line 213)

For `OutputTokenCount` it returns `prices.get("output")` directly. The Terraform variable schema
makes `output` `optional()`, so a `SEED_RATES` entry that legitimately supplies only `input` yields
`None`, and `_rate_for` then skips the seed entirely — output-token pricing becomes unavailable
despite a usable input seed being configured.

## Why they are grouped

Both are in the rate-resolution path, both turn a configuration that the schema permits into a
silently wrong or missing price, and both would be exercised by the same tests. Splitting them
would duplicate the fixture work.

## Why this matters

A wrong or missing rate makes the metered spend figure wrong. That figure is the handler's fast
signal, so an incorrect rate does not fail loudly — it produces a plausible number that is too low
or too high, which is worse than an outage because nothing flags it.

## Source

Advisory findings on Gerrit change 2984 patchset 7, deliberately left unactioned there to keep that
change's scope from growing again after four `LLM-Review -1` rounds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test proves a usage-type body with no region prefix resolves to the correct rate key rather
      than having its leading segment stripped. Verified by that test failing against the current
      implementation first.
- [ ] A test proves a model identifier whose leading hyphen segment is meaningful is not truncated.
      Verified by that test failing against the current implementation first.
- [ ] A test proves a `SEED_RATES` entry supplying only `input` still yields a usable seed rather
      than `None` for output-token pricing, or the code is changed to reject such an entry at load
      time with a named error. Verified by that test passing.
- [ ] Whichever of those two readings is correct — fall back, or refuse the entry — is stated on
      this ticket with its reasoning before the implementation lands. Verified by reading the
      ticket.
- [ ] Branch coverage over `handler.py` remains at 100%. Verified by a coverage run over
      `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap` reporting 0 missing and 0 partial.
compiled_state.title: Bedrock spend cap rate resolution: region-prefix stripping and a seed entry with no output price both mis-price silently
